transcript.text: Alright everyone, let's get the sign-off meeting started. We've got the awards-show tribute scheduled for the main stage during the live broadcast on Friday at 8:00 PM, and the current draft has two indoor flame jets at the upstage edge with the audience beginning 2 meters from the stage. Before I can approve the final effects plan and we can get the production certificate issued, I need to go through the review agenda. Rafael, can you confirm the safety configuration for the flame jets and audience distance? And Jules, I'll need you to confirm the insurance requirements as well. Let's work through this so we can get everything signed off.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag something important before we go further. After inspecting the stage with the fire marshal this morning, I received written event approval for cold-spark units only — exactly four units, positioned at least 3 meters from the audience, operated by a licensed effects operator. The current draft calling for two indoor flame jets with the audience at 2 meters does not match this approval. Also, the approval hasn't been uploaded to the production file yet.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag something on the insurance side. I confirmed with the insurer yesterday that the show is covered for effects only if the cold-spark plan is attached to a filed special-effects endorsement before the broadcast. The insurer's certificate amendment is still awaiting filing, so the insurance documentation is not yet in place.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Thank you both for flagging these issues. Let me make sure I have this straight. Rafael, you're telling me the written event approval only covers four cold-spark units at least 3 meters from the audience with a licensed operator — not the two indoor flame jets at 2 meters in the current draft. And that approval hasn't been uploaded to the production file yet. Jules, you're saying the insurer only covers effects if the cold-spark plan is attached to a filed special-effects endorsement before the broadcast, and that endorsement filing is still pending. So the current draft plan doesn't match the written approval, the insurance documentation isn't in place, and the approval itself isn't in the production file yet. Under the venue's production policy, the final effects plan has to match the written approvals and have the required insurance documentation in place before I can approve it and before the production certificate can be issued. I cannot approve the effects plan as it currently stands. We need to revise the plan to match Rafael's written approval — four cold-spark units, 3 meters minimum audience distance, licensed operator — get that approval uploaded to the production file, and get Jules's special-effects endorsement filed before broadcast. Once those are done, I can approve the revised plan and we can proceed with the production certificate. Can both of you commit to getting those items completed?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Yes, I can commit to that. I'll revise the effects plan to match the written approval exactly — four cold-spark units, positioned at least 3 meters from the audience, operated by a licensed effects operator — and I'll get the written approval uploaded to the production file. I'll have both done as soon as possible so we can move forward with the certificate once Jules's endorsement filing is also complete.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Yes, I can commit to that. I'll get the cold-spark plan attached to the special-effects endorsement and ensure the filing is completed before the Friday 8:00 PM broadcast.
